context: Business review dashboard with 8 KPI sparklines embedded in narrative prose, plus a sortable summary table with inline trend sparklines; 24-month synthetic data (Jan 2023–Dec 2024).
first_impression: A polished sparkline-in-text layout that is structurally honest: Y domains are fully data-driven via d3.extent, and the table uses a key function for object constancy during sorting.
what_works: Y scale uses d3.extent(values) with a flat-line guard ([ext-1, ext+1]), so domains adapt to any data — no hardcoded magic numbers. Table rows are keyed by d => d.id, preventing visual corruption on sort, and inverted metrics (churn, tickets) correctly map 'decrease = good' to the green/blue color channel.
what_doesnt: Sparkline Y axes are auto-scaled per series (non-zero baseline), which is appropriate for line trend charts but makes cross-metric magnitude comparison visually impossible — a 5% churn drop and a 50% revenue gain look similarly 'large'. No line.defined() guard exists, so if any value were undefined or NaN, a straight-line gap would silently appear rather than being omitted.
